messages:
Customer-Rep: Hi, getting paged by ZenStream support — they're seeing a steady stream of 429s starting ~08:03 UTC, spikes clustered at top-of-minute. Only affects EU region.
Anita: Can you paste a sample response header from the client?
Customer-Rep: Sure, from their debug capture: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 02 May 2023 08:03:01 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-RPM: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 23
X-Request-Id: r-zz123
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "Requests per minute exceeded"
}
```
Jamal: Noted. That X-RateLimit-RPM=1200 looks like a tenant-level rpm cap. Are they multiplexing many logical users over a small number of connections (HTTP/2)?
Customer-Rep: Yes — they use a worker pool that opens 6 long HTTP/2 streams and fans out 80 logical requests/sec during bursts.
SRE-Oncall: A couple hypotheses: 1) minute boundary alignment combined with token-bucket refill causes sawtooth (spike at reset). 2) client-side retry policy without jitter produces synchronized retry storms. 3) Our edge ratefolding across AZs can concentrate counts into a single regional bucket briefly.
Support-Bot: Automated check: tenant zenstream (tenant_id: z-44) has sustained RPM=1150, short bursts to ~2200 at 08:03:00 UTC. Recent config: per-tenant cap 1200 rpm, burst window 2s.
Anita: Repro steps we should ask the customer to run: reduce concurrency to 20, add jitter to exponential backoff, and run a 2-minute test across minute boundaries. Example curl (serial) to test: 
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 40); do \
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ \
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" &\
  sleep 0.5
done; wait
```
DevX-Mike: Also request their client library version — older SDKs sometimes retry on 5xx/429 immediately with no jitter. If they're on the open-source SDK, v0.9.2 had a missing jitter bug.
Jamal: Short-term mitigation options for customer: 1) temporary quota bump on Dedicated proxy (if enterprise) for next 24h, 2) enable edge smoothing (we can route a % of their traffic to a secondary region), 3) apply server-side per-connection throttling to spread tokens.
Customer-Rep: Customer asked for recommended backoff settings. What do we suggest?
SRE-Oncall: Recommend: initial_backoff=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff=10s, add randomized jitter +/-30%. Cap total concurrency client-side to avoid bucket depletion. Also advise token refill spread: avoid aligning heavy jobs on minute boundaries (add small random delay to scheduled jobs).
Anita: I ran a quick query on metrics: the 08:03 spike coincides with 3 customers doing bulk sync within same minute window. SRE-Oncall — can you temporarily enable tenant-level smoothing for z-44?
SRE-Oncall: On it. Enabling smoothing (50% reroute to eu-west-2) — will take ~30s. Will monitor for 3 minutes.
Support-Bot: Change applied: smoothing enabled for tenant z-44. Telemetry: expected blended RPM lowered by ~40%.
Customer-Rep: Customer confirmed reduced 429s after smoothing; still see occasional ones at 08:05. They implemented concurrency cap and jitter too.
Jamal: Follow-ups: 1) offer a short-term quota bump if they expect continued heavy syncs 2) recommend SDK upgrade doc + sample backoff snippet 3) add an eval in Console showing minute-aligned spike visualization for tenants.
DevX-Mike: I'll draft an example snippet for SDK v1.x with jitter and post in the ticket.
Anita: I'll keep this thread open until two hours of stable telemetry. Thanks all :thumbsup:
